task: STAGE-DEPENDENT length mis-fires: 0x17 (vertex vs compute) and 0x04 (mesh vs fragment)
summary: Both stage-dependent 0x17 and 0x04 collisions ARE statically disambiguable by a fixed byte signature (no context-dependent limitation needed). (1) VERTEX 0x17 coordinate-transform (`17 22 a2 b0`) is distinguished from COMPUTE 0x17 simd_ballot (`17 07/17 .. 54/56`) by byte+2==0xa2 & byte+3==0xb0; its length is 10 -- the SAME as simd_ballot -- so the desync was NOT a length error but a MISSING DESCRIPTOR (instr_length returned 10 via the else branch, but no length-10 descriptor matched the vertex bytes, so decode_one halted AT the 0x17). Fixed with an explicit stage branch + a vtx_coord_xform descriptor. (2) MESH 0x04 output-store source (`04 SS e7 02`) IS a genuine length mis-fire: the flat fragment centroid rule `0x04 -> 8` over-read it by 6, swallowing the following device_store head + a `0f 06` pop_reconverge. Split to length 2 gated on byte+2==0xe7 && byte+3==0x02, plus a mesh_out_src descriptor.

lengthRuleEdits.location: instr_length(), inside `if b0 == 0x17:` block, before the final `return 10`
lengthRuleEdits.note: Length UNCHANGED (10, same as compute simd_ballot). This is a documentary stage-split so the vertex form is explicitly recognized; the load-bearing fix is the vtx_coord_xform descriptor below. Compute simd_ballot keeps byte+1-low-nibble-7 / byte+2 0x54|0x56; compute sh_down is byte+2==0x82; none carry byte+2==0xa2, so the split is exclusive.

lengthRuleEdits.location: instr_length(), immediately BEFORE the `# Fragment sample-position ... return 8 centroid-position read` rule
lengthRuleEdits.note: GENUINE length correction. The `04 SS e7 02` op feeds the immediately-following 14-byte device_store (0xe7 leader at byte+2, its 0x02 sub-byte at byte+3), so the 0x04 op is only 2 bytes. Gate excludes the fragment centroid read (byte+2 != 0xe7), get_sr (byte+3 low-nibble 6, matched earlier), sr_read_wide (byte+1>=0x80, matched earlier) and rt_intersect (byte+1==0xea).

descriptors.semantics: VERTEX-stage coordinate / position transform op. Reads a vertex-array / constant-indexed coordinate and produces the clip-space position or a varying coordinate. byte+2==0xa2, byte+3==0xb0 are the fixed operand-selector pair that statically distinguish it from the compute-stage 0x17 simd_ballot (byte+2==0x54/0x56) with which it shares byte0 and length (10). The operand bytes are left raw (the coordinate-select sequence is not reconstructed, clean-room rule 5).

Length 10 bracketed: the next op leader begins exactly 10 bytes later (root 0x21 in deriv-shaped VS, root 0x00 in discard-shaped VS).

descriptors.semantics: MESH-stage compact source op feeding the immediately-following device store (byte+2==0xe7) of a mesh vertex/primitive output. Occupies the same structural slot as the 8-byte sr_read_wide (mesh_point `04 88 06 ..`) but is a distinct 2-byte compact encoding (byte+1 < 0x80). byte+1 left raw.
descriptors.provenance: OWN-SHADER (EXP-M4-13 R5, byte-diff/bracket, NOT HW-dispatch-validated): mesh corpus mesh-stage hex (mesh_transform/tri/line/maxout/grid3d/amplify_dyn/obj_reduce/payload_large/pervertex_wide); length 2 bracketed by an if_push (0f 05 54 01) before and a 14-byte device_store (e7 02 54|64 ..) after in every sample; mesh_transform own recompile byte-checked.

replaces: instr_length 0x17 flat `else return 10` (simd_ballot) -- now split so the vertex byte+2==0xa2/byte+3==0xb0 form is named vtx_coord_xform (still 10); compute simd_ballot path unchanged.
instr_length 0x04 flat `return 8` centroid-position read -- now preceded by the mesh `byte+2==0xe7 && byte+3==0x02 -> 2` split; the fragment centroid path (byte+2 != 0xe7) is unchanged.
notes: 0x17 was a MISSING-DESCRIPTOR desync, not a length error: instr_length already returned 10 for the vertex form (via the compute else branch), but decode_one found no length-10 descriptor matching `17 22 a2 b0 ..` and halted at the 0x17. The stage split is therefore documentary for length but load-bearing for identity; adding vtx_coord_xform is what actually clears the halt.

0x04 mesh op WAS a real length mis-fire (8 vs 2). Direct trace confirms the `0f 06` pop_reconverge is now preserved: mesh_transform @44 `04 01`=mesh_out_src(2) -> @46 device_store(14) -> @60 `0f 06 24 01 00 00` pop_reconverge(6), instead of the old 8-byte over-read that swallowed the store head + reconverge.

The task cited `root 0x24 x11` for the 0x04 swallow. In the committed DB the mesh 0x04 does not actually reach a 0x24 landing -- it HALTS at the 0x04 itself (no descriptor for the mis-lengthed 8-byte value), so the swallow is latent. The length-2 fix prevents any swallow regardless; the reconverge preservation is verified directly by trace rather than via a 0x24 root.

Downstream roots are the task's predicted genuine next-ops and are OUT OF SCOPE for this task: after the vertex 0x17 decodes, deriv-shaped VS halt on 0x21 (`21 82 a6 b0`) and discard-shaped VS halt on 0x00 (`00 04 00 00`); after the mesh 0x04 decodes, the mesh stages advance ~50-150 bytes and halt on 0x02 (`02 88 21 80 26 a0 ..`, a sibling coord op with byte+3==0xa0). These are separate follow-up items.

Mesh byte+1 selector values observed: 0x01 (mesh_transform/tri/grid3d/amplify_dyn/obj_reduce/payload_large/pervertex_wide), 0x04 (mesh_line), 0x20 (mesh_maxout). Left raw; likely the set_primitive_count / lane value. The byte+2==0xe7 && byte+3==0x02 gate generalizes to any selector value (does not hard-code the observed set).
